title: Leray: composition of derived functors
statement:
For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ and
$E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\cong\RGamma\bigl(Y_{\Et},Rf_*E\bigr)
$$

in $\Dplus(\mathbf Z)$, compatible with the functorialities (this is
the composition of the derived functors of
$\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)=\Gamma(Y_{\Et},-)\circ f_*$).

proof.text: Choose an integer a below the cohomology of E. The abelian-sheaf categories on X and Y have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] choose E ≅ QI with I a complex of injective abelian sheaves, I^r=0 for r<a. The complex I is K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], every f_*I^r is injective; additivity of f_* [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] preserves zero objects, so f_*I is bounded below by a and is K-injective by the same representative lemma. By the derived-direct-image definition, Rf_*E ≅ Q(f_*I).

By [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], derived global sections on X are represented by Γ(X,I) and those of Rf_*E on Y by Γ(Y,f_*I), since both I and f_*I are K-injective. In degree r, the direct-image formula gives Γ(Y,f_*I^r)=I^r(Y×_Y X). The projection Y×_Y X→X is an isomorphism: its inverse is the unique map with projections f and id_X, and both inverse identities follow from the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Restriction along this isomorphism gives I^r(Y×_Y X)≅I^r(X). Naturality of restriction in sheaf morphisms makes these maps commute with I's differentials. Thus they form a chain isomorphism Γ(Y,f_*I)≅Γ(X,I). Its inverse in Dplus(Z) is the asserted comparison.

For a morphism E→E', choose bounded-below injective representatives I,I'. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] it has a unique representing homotopy class h:I→I'. The derived-direct-image definition computes Rf_* on this class by f_*h. The degreewise sections isomorphism in Step 2 commutes with h, since both paths apply h to the same restricted section. Additive termwise global sections and direct image respect homotopies, so this square descends to the derived category. A change of injective representative is a homotopy equivalence by the same bijection (represent the inverse derived isomorphism and use injectivity of Q on Hom); the square just proved identifies the comparisons for the two choices. Hence the comparison is canonical and natural in E. For composable scheme maps X→Y→Z, the two sections identifications restrict along the iterated fibre product projections. The unique isomorphism between Z×_Z(Y×_Y X) and X preserves these projections [def-pc-fibre-product], so the composite restriction is the single restriction to X. For an identity scheme map that projection is the identity. Applying these equalities degreewise to I proves composition and identity compatibility. If RGamma is taken in its unbounded convention, [lem-kun-rgamma-unbounded-bounded] identifies both computations naturally with that convention.

lean.statement: def rightDerivedGlobalSectionsLerayPlus {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (E : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) : (Sheaf.Γ X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj E ≅ ((Sheaf.Γ Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj (((f)_*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj E))
lean.note: The upstream generic composition isomorphism requires an explicit PreservesInjectiveObjects instance that does not synthesize in this specialization. This module installs the structural instance from the étale upper-star/lower-star adjunction and states the scheme-level bounded-below Leray isomorphism directly, with all functors and the canonical underived comparison explicit.
